name: Griva bhedha (neck warm-up)
summary: The classical neck movements — side to side and turning — done slowly as a warm-up before any dance practice.
setup: Sit or stand tall facing the phone, about 1.5 m away, camera at chest height. Slide the head from side to side (sundari), then turn it left and right, keeping the shoulders completely still.
brief: Sit or stand tall. Slide the head from side to side (sundari), then turn it left and right, keeping the shoulders completely still.
why: Facing the camera, the head sliding across the shoulder line is counted. Whether the movement is a slide or a tilt is too subtle for a phone to separate.
calibrationPose: Sitting or standing tall, head centred, shoulders level.
tempo: Two seconds each way; never fast.
progression: Larger range once it is comfortable; add the eye movements.
regression: Smaller range; seated with the back supported.
contraindications: Dizziness, pain shooting into the arm, or any neck injury not yet assessed.

faults.label: Shoulders moving with the head
faults.tip: The shoulders stay square and level. If they follow the head, the movement has left the neck.

faults.label: Tilting instead of sliding
faults.tip: Sundari is a sideways slide, ears staying level — not a tilt of the head toward the shoulder.

faults.label: Moving too quickly
faults.tip: This is a warm-up for a joint with a lot of small structures. Speed is how people strain it.

faults.label: Forcing the end of the range
faults.tip: Warm-ups move through the easy range. Pushing into the end is a stretch, and a different thing.

guide.surface: Sitting tall on a stool, or standing.
guide.stop: Dizziness, or any pain or tingling into the arm.
guide.cannotSee: Whether the head is sliding or tilting, and the eye movements that go with it.

points.t: Slides sideways with the ears staying level; then turns left and right.
Chin stays level throughout — no nodding.
